instruction.text: Let’s take a look at a case study about flood management in the UK. Select Morpeth to learn more.

feedback.finish: Morpeth is a town in North-East England located close to the River Wansbeck. The area has a lot of intense flooding, which led to the local government creating a flood management scheme.

instruction.text: You’re speaking to a Morpeth local. Fill in the gaps in the conversation.

atoms.b: That must have been in 2008. Over 400 residents were evacuated, and we all ((++sheltered danced)) in the town hall.
We had such a huge amount of ((++rainfall earthquakes)) that the river overflowed!
Oh no, that’s awful! What happened to people from the ((++town ocean))?
Many people were forced out of their ((++homes clothes)) and had to stay in temporary shelters while ((++rebuilding destruction)) efforts took place.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: Morpeth already had some flood defences in place, but they introduced new measures in response to the damage caused by the 2008 floods.
For example, they increased the height of the flood walls around the town and constructed embankments to protect the housing estates closest to the river.

hint.text: An embankment is a thick wall of earth that keeps water from a river or the sea from flooding into towns.
hint.label: Embankments

atoms.text: In addition, Morpeth built a large dam upstream. This only lets through a small amount of water at a time, which the town’s defences can manage safely.
